name: Mike Crapo

issue_poll.name: Boise State University 8th Annual Idaho Public Policy Survey, Nov 10–17, 2022; plus Pew Research Center, Oct 10–16, 2022
issue_poll.note: No ranked pre-election Idaho poll found. Ranks 1–6 come from the Boise State battery's items that a majority rated 8–10 in importance (education 72%, jobs/economy 64%, housing 61%, health care 60%, taxes 54%, environment 52%). Transportation (42%) was left out. Ranks 7–10 come from Pew's national 'very important' list, skipping items already covered and 'future of democracy' (no vote can test it): energy 61%, violent crime 61%, elections/voting 58%, gun policy 57%. Pew source: https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2022/10/PP_2022.10.20_midterms-economy_REPORT.pdf

issues.position: Cut federal spending; pass a Balanced Budget Amendment
issues.note: No floor vote on a Balanced Budget Amendment this term. Vote source: https://www.crapo.senate.gov/media/newsreleases/crapo-statement-on-senate-passed-rescissions-package

caveats: The issue poll is a state-legislature priorities battery fielded just after Election Day, combined with national Pew data. Abortion (Pew 56%) and immigration (54%) fall just outside the top 10.
Campaign issue page was last updated April 2022. Positions come from it, a campaign mailer and the Oct 3, 2022 debate.
H.R.7024 is scored against him on both housing and taxes; most Republicans opposed it, but it expanded both tax cuts and the housing credit.
Roll call numbers are not confirmed for H.R.4 (July 17, 2025), S.3386 (Dec 11, 2025) or S.J.Res.7 (Mar 29, 2023).
The environment position (oppose EPA farm rules) is broad; it is scored only on the WOTUS disapproval vote.
